name: Peter Burgoyne
heroAlt: Peter Burgoyne standing beside the sea in warm evening light
tributeHtml:
A life shaped by purpose, service and quiet determination.
Peter gave his time, skills and care generously.
shareDescription: A personal memorial song created from Peter’s story.
lyrics:
Born in February, in Derby town,
Peter learned to work and stand his ground.
From Chapel Street Market in his younger days,
He built his life in quiet, steadfast ways.

London became where his path would unfold,
With a curious mind and a spirit so bold.
Whatever the challenge, whatever was new,
He met it with purpose and always saw it through.

You made a life of purpose,
A life both strong and true.
You gave your time so freely
In everything you would do.

A husband, dad and grandad,
A loyal, trusted friend.
The lessons that you gave us
Will stay with us always.

At Burton’s dance hall, beneath the lights,
Peter met Diane on those London nights.
Caravan holidays, sea air and song,
Two people discovering where they belonged.

They married in June in the summer of ’70,
Then built their home and their family.
Karl, then Ross, then Louise came along,
And Peter stood beside them, dependable and strong.

He taught them to swim and be safe in the tide,
And watched their confidence grow by his side.
Then grandchildren came and brought joy to his days,
Each one dearly loved in their own special way.

Buster and Isla, Beau and Jolie,
Then Honey completed the family tree.
He watched every milestone with grandfather’s pride,
Content just to listen and stand by their side.

His lifeguard training opened a door,
To teach and to help and to give even more.
He worked with the swimmers, the young and disabled,
Sharing his knowledge whenever he was able.

He served on the Thames through the darkness and rain,
Keeping watch over London again and again.
At concerts and crossings, wherever the need,
He offered his time through his actions and deeds.

From Baxter Hoare to the Greenwich days,
Peter kept learning and finding new ways.
And when one door closed, he would start something new,
Finding another good job he could do.

From poolside to post room, friendships were made,
With stories and laughter that brightened each day.
Whatever the role and wherever he went,
He gave it his best and was quietly content.

He stacked up the wood for the cold winter days,
And worked in his boiler suit, dusty and grey.
The sound of the saw would ring out from the shed,
With plans for the next useful job in his head.

The neighbours would smile when a skip came in view,
For Peter could see what might still be of use.
Where others saw rubbish, he always saw more,
A purpose worth saving and bringing back home.

You made a life of purpose,
A life both full and true.
You gave your strength so freely
In everything you would do.

A husband, dad and grandad,
A loyal, trusted friend.
The love and time you gave us
Will never truly end.
rememberingParagraphs: Peter was hardworking, practical and endlessly curious. From his early days in Derby and London to the many roles he took on throughout his life, he met change with determination and was always ready to learn something new.

He was a devoted husband to Diane, a proud father to Karl, Ross and Louise, and a much-loved grandad to Buster, Isla, Beau, Jolie and Honey. His friendships, his love of music, his swimming and lifesaving work, and his years serving on the Thames all reflected the loyalty and generosity he brought to the people around him.

Peter had a gift for seeing usefulness where others might not, whether in a new skill, a practical job or a piece of wood rescued for winter. The time he gave, the lessons he shared and the steady way he stood beside those he loved remain part of the family life he helped to build.
closingLine: A life of purpose, remembered with love.
